Great food and good value
May 2017 • Family
We called this restaurant the windmill restaurant because of it's trade mark windmill which others in the chain also display. The restaurant is deceptively large with several function rooms tucked away. There is a large eating space downstairs and an upstairs area that's divided into 2. There is an outside balcony that overlooks part of the down stairs area and a stage and an enclosed.area. The enclosed area is air conditioned. We ate there about 6 time, always upstairs, sometimes inside sometimes out. They have bands and singers to provide entertainment and on the whole were pretty good. If that was too much you can move inside where it's quieter although they do have a trio (guitar, drum and sax) who do the occasional song and happy birthdays. Probably should get to the main point and that is the food is very very good and at a reasonable price that makes it good value for money. The menu is also quite extensive. Drink prices are fairly standard. I agree with another reviewer that the staff are not great smilers, but I found they are very helpful and once I got talking to them in broken English and miserable efforts at Vietnamese the smiles came. I'd recommend the pork ribs on bamboo and the seafood spring rolls, but there's lots of other great dishes. I'd eat upstairs.

Seafood Dinner
Feb 2017 • Friends
This restaurant was recommended to us as the best seafood place to eat in Saigon. After locating the restaurant we were greeted by a very nice lady and given a table (after a couple of locals were made to move to another table to fit us in a total of 4 people in our group). The service is not to be recommended after finally being able to order some drinks there was another delay in ordering our meals. After waiting one & half hours we had received 2 dishes out of a total of 5 ordered. Problem we believe is that not all of us ordered seafood, only one person did. Kept asking how long & being told it was going to be another 5 minutes. Decided to pay for what we had and to leave. 
The 2 meals delivered were quite nice but the service leaves a lot to be desired. 
Golden rule of delivering meals is to make sure that all meals for the same course are delivered at same time.

Eat The Seafood Avoid The Rest
Mar 2016 • Business
This restaurant is considered an institution with the locals and tourists alike in Saigon. The Ngoc Suong location we visited has a beautiful and grand design. It was designed with a nautical theme with a grand entrance and spiral staircase. 

We seafood on the menu are the star of this restaurant. We orded fresh crayfish, steamed chicken and grilled beef. The crayfish was delicious while the other proteins were simply adequate. This is a seafood restaurant and I would recommend that you stick with seafood to get the best that Ngoc Suong has to offer. 

The live band that played during our dinner was a nice touch. I would return the next time I am in Saigon but I would strictly stay wih the seafood.
